auditor: Claude (fresh-context subagent, same family as the preparer)
method: For each of the 44 sampled records (19 targeted, 25 random, from audit-sample.json), every evidence passage was located in the cached source text (tools.mjs text/grep/page) or, for sources without a cache, in the dataset passages for the source's datasetSource in data/evidence.json; a context window of roughly 500-900 characters either side was read, and for surveys the body (question wording, aggregation method, conditions) was searched as needed. Each record was checked on the eight points of the brief. All 53 records' qualification, eventNote, hedge, conditions and date notes were read for rule 8. verification.json and review notes were not opened. Quotation matching was done on whitespace- and quote-normalised lowercase text; PDF text-layer damage is noted per record.

results.finding: Both quotations are in the jmc.stanford.edu transcription (text layer drops the "fi" ligature: "signi cant", "arti cial"). Conditional ("if a carefully selected group ... for a summer") and hedge ("We think that") kept; horizon recorded as worded, with the 1956 summer taken from the first sentence and quoted separately.

Operations Research 6:1-10 (1958)" and "our (four) predictions". Internally consistent.

results.finding: All three Michie passages are in the 1986 scan (text-layer damage: dropped spaces, "someofthe", "machineintelligence"; figure legend symbols render as ": ,"); printed p. 146 matches. Quotation verbatim. Two wording points: (1) the qualification asserts "the wording is his paraphrase of the letters", but the source only reports them in indirect speech without quotation marks, so whether it is paraphrase or close quotation is not established; (2) the preceding sentence frames these as examples of "wild predictions regarding the future of robot development" still being made, which the record omits although it changes how the report is read.
results.suggested_fix: Replace "the wording is his paraphrase of the letters" with "reported in indirect speech, without quotation marks". Add: "Lighthill introduces the examples as "wild predictions regarding the future of robot development" (preceding sentence); that characterisation is his."

results.finding: Quotation verbatim; event and horizon ("by the year 2000") as worded; hedge "awe-inspiring possibilities suggest themselves" kept. Same wording points as the companion record: "in his words" overstates what is known, and Lighthill's framing ("wild predictions") is omitted.
Verbatim; condition (100 Tops, 12 or 18 month doubling) kept; next sentence ("the best experimental supercomputers ... not necessarily the computers available to AI researchers") correctly added.

Abstract quotation verbatim (text layer: "highlevel"). The survey question was conditional: "assume that human scientific activity continues without major negative disruption" (p. 9, p. 17), and HLMI is defined as one "that can carry out most human professions at least as well as a typical human" (p. 4); neither is recorded, although the scope asks for question framing where the report states it.
results.suggested_fix: Add conditions: "Assume ... human scientific activity continues without major negative disruption" (question 2), and an eventNote with the HLMI definition (p. 4). Optionally note the overall median for 50% is 2040 (p. 10), the abstract's "2040-2050" being its own summary.

results.finding: The abstract's "Experts expect that systems will move on to superintelligence in less than 30 years thereafter" summarises a probability answer: the body gives a median of 75% (mean 62%) for "within 30 years" and 10% for "within 2 years" (p. 12; restated p. 14 "in 2 years (10%) to 30 years (75%)"), on a question that begins "Assume for the purpose of this question that such HLMI will at some point exist". The record has probability null and no condition, so it reads as a firm expectation.
results.suggested_fix: Set probability to the report's figures (median 75% within 30 years; 10% within 2 years; mean 62% and 19%), add the condition "Assume ... such HLMI will at some point exist", and note the question's definition ("machine intelligence that greatly surpasses the performance of any human in most professions").

results.finding: Verbatim; "Taking the mean over each individual, the aggregate forecast gave a 50% chance of HLMI occurring within 45 years" (p. 2) supports the statistic; interval kept as years from 2016 (figure axis "Years from 2016").
Verbatim; separate question correctly noted.

Quotation verbatim. The qualification compresses two separate statements: the abstract says respondents "newly contacted in 2019 expressed similar beliefs" to the Grace et al. respondents, and that for recontacted participants the 50% date "shifted from 2062 to 2076, although this change is not statistically significant likely due to the small size of our panel sample". "Does not differ significantly from the 2016 survey" blurs these.
results.suggested_fix: Replace with: "The report says newly contacted 2019 respondents expressed similar beliefs to the 2016 survey's; for recontacted panel respondents the 50% year moved from 2062 to 2076, a change it reports as not statistically significant."

Matches the dataset passage. (1) "given the current rate of progress" is a stated condition but is recorded in neither conditions nor hedge. (2) The source date kind "captured" is used for 2000-08-31, which is the page's "Updated" revision date; the capture is 2000-12-04 (the dataset uses basis "revision"). (3) "the author has since repudiated this text, which the dataset records separately": the dataset claim found (yk-y22-sl4-2000-11-13...) says only that he no longer holds a specific belief about objective morality, not that he repudiated the text or its timeline.
results.suggested_fix: Add condition "given the current rate of progress"; set date kind to "revised" (Updated 08/31/2000) with capture date 2000-12-04; replace the repudiation clause with the specific dataset claim and its scope, or remove it.

results.finding: Verbatim; "could be", "as little as" and "although it could also be considerably further out" kept; restatement of the 2024 essay correctly noted.

wording_sweep.issue: "the wording is his paraphrase of the letters" asserts more than the source shows (indirect speech, no quotation marks); Lighthill's own framing of the examples as "wild predictions" is omitted.
wording_sweep.suggested_fix: "Reported in indirect speech, without quotation marks." Add Lighthill's framing, attributed to him.

wording_sweep.issue: "in his words" carries the same overstatement.
wording_sweep.suggested_fix: "Lighthill's unnamed report of letters he received, in indirect speech."

wording_sweep.issue: "the author has since repudiated this text" is broader than the dataset record it points to (he no longer holds a specific belief about objective morality); it reads as a statement about the person and the forecast.
wording_sweep.suggested_fix: Name the specific dataset claim and its scope, or remove the clause.

wording_sweep.issue: "does not differ significantly from the 2016 survey" merges two statements of the abstract (similar beliefs of new respondents; non-significant 2062-to-2076 shift for the recontacted panel).
wording_sweep.suggested_fix: State both as the report words them.

wording_sweep.issue: Does not say that the cited essay's own horizon ("as early as 2026") differs from the submission's ("late 2026 or early 2027").
wording_sweep.suggested_fix: Add the essay's horizon in its words.

wording_sweep.issue: "The statement is part of a funding proposal" is factual but may be read as implying a motive for the optimism; low priority.
wording_sweep.suggested_fix: "The statement is part of the proposal for the 1956 summer study." (optional)

wording_sweep.issue: Verbal hedges ("could", "may", "we expect", "it's conceivable", "we find it plausible", "strikingly plausible") are stored in the `probability` field in many forecast records (e.g. pr-f-amodei-2026-one-to-two-years, pr-f-openai-2023-governance-ten-years, pr-f-anthropic-2025-late-2026-early-2027), while other records put comparable wording in `hedge`. pack.md renders them under "Probability or confidence", which a reader may take as a stated probability.
wording_sweep.suggested_fix: Keep `probability` for numerical or explicitly probabilistic statements and move verbal hedges to `hedge`, or relabel the rendered field "Stated confidence (words)".
